title: Strayed Stock By Ford
text:
One red-and-white brahmin wandered off at dawn. Brass tag
on the left harness. Return it to the yard, not the
butcher. A reasonable finder will get a reasonable
payment. An unreasonable finder will see me in person.

title: Freight Rates This Week
text:
Small parcels ride with the line when the line runs. Bulk
loads require a scale ticket. Nobody is paying for water
weight in wet sacks. Speak to the freight agent before
leaving goods beside the shed.

title: Burial On The Hill
text:
A burial will be held beyond the west fence after the
afternoon bell. Keep carts off the upper path until the
ground has been set. Those carrying a shovel may bring it
and be useful.

title: Boil The River Water
text:
River water is not fit for drinking this week. Draw from
the town pump or boil your own until it has rolled hard.
The clinic has had enough of folks who cannot wait for a
kettle.

title: Gate Duty And Hours
text:
The west gate opens with daylight. After dark, announce
yourself from the bench and wait for the deputy. Anyone
rattling the latch after the second bell is likely to meet
the wrong end of his patience.

title: Wagon For Sale
text:
Four wheels, three good hubs, and one argument that has
lasted since planting. Needs an axle pin and two strong
shoulders. No offers of promises, chickens or future
freight. Ask at the freight yard.

title: Greenwater Short Of Flour
text:
Carters heading toward Greenwater report low meal and
flour. Beans or dry grain will fetch a proper price if
weighed honestly. Leave your figures with the trading post
before the line opens again.

title: Red Hollow Work Halted
text:
The Red Hollow mine remains closed by its own overseer. Do
not mistake a locked gate for abandoned property. Anyone
entering without leave should be ready to answer to the
mine owners rather than the town.

title: Track Damage Report
text:
A handcar from Iron Junction found disturbed rail spikes
beyond the northern cutting. Stay clear of loose sleepers.
Report bent fishplates or fresh tool marks to the Warden
office. Do not try repairs with a kitchen hammer.

title: Pump Work On Sunday
text:
The hand pump needs new leather in the plunger. Water will
be drawn from stored barrels during the repair. Every
household takes its share. Anyone who empties a barrel
before breakfast may help carry the next one.

title: Lost Pair Of Boots
text:
Missing from the clinic back step: one pair of boots, size
large, patched at the left heel. They were drying, not
abandoned. Return them and nothing more will be said about
the feet that walked off in them.

title: Market Weights Checked
text:
The trading scales were checked on the 9th of May. Weights
belong on the counter, not beneath it. Buyers and sellers
may request a second measure without being called liars.
Repeated requests are still irritating.

title: Owen Pritchard Greeting
text: If you are bleeding, the clinic is east of the office.

title: Owen Pritchard Greeting
text: I have had enough surprises for one morning.

title: Owen Pritchard Greeting
text: A clean gun says little about the hand holding it.

title: Owen Pritchard Greeting
text: There is a bench. It has outlived three deputies.

title: Ada Pike Greeting
text: That barrel has seen better decades.

title: Ada Pike Greeting
text: I charge for repairs, not compliments.

title: Ada Pike Greeting
text:
Keep your fingers off the spring unless you enjoy counting
nine.

title: Ada Pike Greeting
text: The book says what I am owed. My face says less.

title: Silas Vane Greeting
text: A fair price is one both parties remember fondly.

title: Silas Vane Greeting
text: Welcome in. Please leave the mud on the other side.

title: Silas Vane Greeting
text: The road brings customers and takes them away again.

title: Silas Vane Greeting
text: I sell most things. Certainty costs extra.

title: Miriam Keene Greeting
text: Sit down before you fall down.

title: Miriam Keene Greeting
text: I mend people. I do not make them sensible.

title: Miriam Keene Greeting
text: The boil water notice is not decoration.

title: Miriam Keene Greeting
text: Bandages are for wounds, not bruised pride.

title: Jonah Talbot Greeting
text: The gate latch sticks. The rules do not.

title: Jonah Talbot Greeting
text: I can write your name. Spelling takes longer.

title: Jonah Talbot Greeting
text: Sheriff says I should watch the road. I do.

title: Jonah Talbot Greeting
text: It is not a threat if I whistle first. Probably.

title: Corwin Haskell Greeting
text: Five crates came in. Four signed out. That concerns me.

title: Corwin Haskell Greeting
text: Please do not lean on the scales.

title: Corwin Haskell Greeting
text: The freight book is dry. That is my victory today.

title: Corwin Haskell Greeting
text: The door marked freight is the freight door.

title: Nell Grateful
text: That wagon still rolls because someone stopped.

title: Nell Grateful
text: Abel says you were quick. He rarely says anything quick.

title: Nell Grateful
text: I owe you one favor, not a lifetime of freight.

title: Nell Grateful
text: The brahmin took fright. I cannot blame them.

title: Nell Bitter
text: I saw you take the long way around.

title: Nell Bitter
text: Watching costs nothing. It saved you a fortune.

title: Nell Bitter
text: Abel remembers who stood by. He remembers quietly.

title: Nell Bitter
text: Roads do not choose sides. People do.

title: Nell Cold
text: I counted my missing goods and your share.

title: Nell Cold
text: Do not ask for trade at my wagon.

title: Nell Cold
text: You knew where those men stood. I saw it.

title: Nell Cold
text: If you want forgiveness, try buying it elsewhere.

title: Unfinished Letter Home
text:
I have enough food for the return road, if the wagons keep
moving. The hills look fine when they are not standing
between you and supper. I meant to send this before we
took the lower grade. If I miss market day, please do not
sell the warm coat. The nights here have a way of finding
your collar.

title: A Firemans Grade Note
text:
Lower grade ran wet again. The engine pulled hard near the
bend and the rear wagons seemed to press. I asked for an
inspection before the next run. The yard said to write it
down, so here it is. I know the difference between an old
machine grumbling and a machine asking for help.

title: Freight Bill Copy
text:
Consignee: Mercy Crossing freight shed. Three parcels of
lamp oil, two sacks of dry grain and one box of tools.
Deliver by the line, subject to safe passage. Any missing
seal must be noted before unloading. Freight charges are
due when the goods are weighed and counted. No
substitution on the line without the agent signing for it.

title: Small Drawing Found
text:
A child drew a wagon, two wide-headed cattle, a river and
a crooked bridge. The sun is below the river.

title: Names In Pencil
text:
A list of workers for the lower-grade shift. One name is
heavily crossed out. Beside it someone wrote: Not going.
The rest of the names are ordinary workmen and carters,
with no explanation. The page is damp where it was folded
and bears no signature.
